decisions.rationale: The author directly asserts future delivery of a concrete draft without a qualification.
The author organisation directly undertakes to supply a concrete log in a future period.
This asks the recipient to make a register available; it is not the author promising delivery.
The author explicitly guarantees that an author-owned work item will reach the recipient by a future deadline.
The author organisation gives an explicit assurance of future sharing of a concrete draft.
The sentence attributes the delivery statement to another person and her team.
The author organisation identifies its engineering team as the owner of an unqualified future delivery.
The delivery assertion occurs inside an earlier message quoted by the customer, not a current author undertaking.
The author states a definite plan to hand over a concrete runbook at a future meeting.
The author organisation expressly commits its finance team to delivering a concrete sheet tomorrow.
The author organisation directly asserts a future package handover; the call specifies timing rather than a delivery condition.
The passive construction explicitly assigns future delivery of the runbook to the author team.
Calling the arrival an estimate qualifies the prospective delivery rather than asserting it firmly.
Present-progressive wording with tomorrow states an unqualified future delivery by the author organisation.
This explicitly negates the author organisation sending the agenda; it does not state a delivery intention.
The prospective delivery is quoted from a forwarded note, not adopted as a current author promise.
The question asks the recipient organisation to supply its log.
The author explicitly promises that a concrete summary will be received from the author organisation before an event.
The author asks the recipient to send a worksheet.
The author team is explicitly the source of a concrete glossary going out at a future time.
The author asserts future sharing of a complete agenda; the fronted event phrase sets the deadline.
The author directly undertakes to deliver the sheet to the recipient inbox by a future deadline.
This describes a diary record of an earlier promise, rather than making a current delivery assertion.
The sentence describes a completed delivery, not a prospective one.
The author explicitly withholds a firm promise about future delivery. It leaves delivery uncertain rather than asserting that no delivery will happen.
Counterfactual ownership describes a hypothetical action rather than a current future delivery plan or undertaking.
The sentence reports an earlier promise recorded in account history.
Future upload is expressly conditional on translator sign-off.
The handover is described as already completed before a past call.
The author organisation explicitly commits to future provision of a concrete register.
The author unconditionally states that the completed register will be made available tomorrow.
This requests a glossary upload from the recipient team.
The author explicitly promises a future glossary upload.
The author describes an aim rather than an unqualified commitment to deliver the sheet.
This is an imperative asking the recipient to deliver a sheet.
Delivery remains pending a billing review, which makes the undertaking conditional.
The recipient is told that a concrete package will arrive from the author at a future time.
The author organisation states an expectation, which is tentative rather than an unqualified delivery assertion.
The author organisation explicitly undertakes to send a concrete worksheet tomorrow.
The author explicitly identifies themselves as the source of a concrete future worksheet delivery.
